stops.note: a Midlands and northern term; Notes and Queries in 1879 reported that in Staffordshire someone who went away from Saturday afternoon to Sunday was 'spending his week-end' there
spread with the Saturday half-holiday won by factory laws such as the 1850 Factory Act; the two-day weekend became standard in the US after Henry Ford adopted a five-day week in 1926

current_meaning: Saturday and Sunday, when many people do not work
